# linux_filesystem (Resource)

Makes sure a device holds a file system, or a swap area, formatting it only when it is empty.

A device that already holds a file system of the requested `type` is used as it is, with its data, like cloud-init does: only its label is changed when needed. A device that holds anything else (another file system, a partition table, an LVM or RAID member...) is an error, unless `overwrite` is set. Destroying the resource leaves the file system and its data in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Formats the partition only if it is empty. If it already holds an ext4
# file system, it is used as it is, with its data.
resource "linux_filesystem" "data" {
  device = linux_partition.data.path
  type   = "ext4"
  label  = "data"

  # Grow the file system with its partition, after enlarging the disk.
  grow = true
  triggers = {
    size = linux_partition.data.size_bytes
  }
}

resource "linux_filesystem" "swap" {
  device = linux_partition.swap.path
  type   = "swap"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device` (String) Device to format, such as `linux_partition.data.path`. The resource waits up to 2 minutes for it to appear.
- `type` (String) File system type: `ext2`, `ext3`, `ext4`, `xfs`, `btrfs`, `vfat`, `swap`. The `mkfs` tool must be installed (`xfsprogs`, `btrfs-progs`, `dosfstools`).

### Optional

- `grow` (Boolean) Grow the file system to the size of the device when the device grows, for instance after enlarging a cloud volume and its partition. Supported for ext2/3/4, and for xfs and btrfs while they are mounted. Defaults to `false`.
- `label` (String) File system label, available as `/dev/disk/by-label/<label>` and `LABEL=<label>` in `linux_mount`. Changing it relabels the file system without formatting it. Defaults to the existing label.
- `mkfs_options` (List of String) Extra arguments for `mkfs`, such as `["-m", "1"]` for ext4. Only used when formatting.
- `overwrite` (Boolean) Erase whatever the device holds and format it, even a file system of the requested type. **This destroys its data.** Only used when the resource is created. Defaults to `false`.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that grow the file system again, when `grow` is set, when they change. Use `{ size = linux_partition.data.size_bytes }` to grow it in the same apply as its partition.

### Read-Only

- `device_size` (Number) Size of the device, in bytes, when the file system was created or last grown.
- `id` (String) Path of the device.
- `uuid` (String) UUID of the file system, to mount it with `UUID=<uuid>`, which does not depend on device names.
